provenance: ADR-032 §b3, the refusal path -- the exact shape tables-refusal-path exists for, re-checked for `images` rather than inherited. A refused envelope (`unsupported` or `failed`) is built by an EARLIER return in extract_items than the success path, so 'the annotation is carried when asked' is a separate claim on that branch and has to be asserted there. aapl-2026-10q is Apple's Q3 FY2026 10-Q (evals/fixtures/README.md), refused by form identity with `unsupported_form`; it carries readable text (83,193 normalized chars) and exactly one , the Apple logo on the cover at raw offset 3117: ``, which normalizes to offset 401, immediately after 'Commission File Number: 001-36743'. WHAT EACH CHECK IS FOR. doc_status + warning_present: the refusal itself must be unchanged by the flag -- adding an annotation must not turn a refusal into a parse. only_items([]): the contract's refusal rule, no best-effort items, restated here because a refusal envelope that grew an items list while growing an images list would be the same defect twice. `item: null` on the image label is the load-bearing half of that: with no items there is no span to fall in, and the containment derivation must answer null rather than crash or invent a code -- the branch nothing else in the image cases reaches, since every other labeled image lands inside some span. images_sane min=max=1 and the full `image` label: the list is really carried and really populated on this branch, not merely present-and-empty. offsets_invariant_under_images: the equality holds on the refusal path too, where the annotation is computed before the refusal is decided. HARD RULE 2 NOTE. tables-refusal-path exists because the first S7 build had a `found` name collision on exactly this path -- the local name for the tables list shadowed something else and the refusal envelope shipped a string where a list belonged, which every other table case missed. S10 reuses that same `found` local in normalize() and adds `imgs` beside it, so the collision class is live again; this case is the guard, and `envelope_shape` (which runs `_images_shape`) plus `images_sane` are both here so a wrong TYPE is caught and not only a wrong value.
